## Observation
In `sweep (windows)` diag run 44593555306 (throwaway branch `w1-diag-opcert-acl`, carrying the plump-smelly-indianabat, undamaging-ashamed-wasp and flowered-nonvalued-mink fixes), `test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` failed. The nested run passed. The sandbox TMPDIR it pointed at still held 13 or more `rebar-opcert-ws-*` job workspaces. 323 of the remaining files were read-only, all under `<ws>\.git\objects\..`.

## Cause
`src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py::discard` removes a job workspace with `shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)`. Git writes loose objects and packs read-only. On Windows, deleting a read-only file fails with PermissionError. `ignore_errors=True` swallows that, so every op-cert job on Windows leaves its workspace (a clone of the ticket store) behind in the host temp dir. POSIX deletes read-only files when the parent dir is writable, so the leak is Windows-only.

## Approach
Rewrite `workspace.discard` to call `shutil.rmtree` WITHOUT `ignore_errors` (with it set, CPython never calls the hook) and with an error hook `_retry_writable(func, path, exc)`:
- The hook acts only when `func` is `os.unlink`, `os.remove` or `os.rmdir` (looked up at hook time); for any other failing call rmtree reports (`os.open`, `os.scandir`, `os.lstat`, `os.close`) it returns at once without retrying. For a removal it runs `os.chmod(path, stat.S_IWRITE | stat.S_IREAD)` on the path that failed, then retries `func(path)` once; any `OSError` from either step is swallowed. Adding the read bit means a directory is never left at 0o200.
- The hook is passed as `onexc=` on Python 3.12+ and `onerror=` on 3.11 (requires-python >= 3.11), selected by `sys.version_info`.
- The whole `rmtree` call is also wrapped in `try/except Exception`, so `discard` stays best-effort and never raises into the job (it runs in the `finally` of `jobs.py`, where an exception would replace the job's result).
- Only the failing path is chmodded. That is enough on Windows, where the read-only attribute sits on the file and the parent dir stays deletable. On POSIX a failure would come from a parent-dir permission, which the hook does not fix, so behaviour there is unchanged apart from one extra chmod attempt after a failure.
- The repo's other helper, `llm/workflow/snapshot.py::_rmtree_writable`, chmods the whole tree to 0o700 before removing. It is not reused, because importing `rebar.llm` into the op-cert service would pull the agents layer into a stdlib-only module.
- Out of scope: workspaces that already leaked on Windows hosts. They are plain temp dirs named `rebar-opcert-ws-*` that the OS temp cleaner or an operator removes; no rebar data is lost.
- No config key, env var or flag.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py` — `discard` and its hook.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_workspace_discard_readonly.py` (new) — tests below.

## Testing
All tests run on every platform and model Windows semantics in the test, without relying on real POSIX directory permissions:
- A tree of writable dirs holding read-only files (mirroring `.git/objects/xx/<sha>`). `os.unlink` is patched with a fake that accepts `(path, *, dir_fd=None)`, stats the target via `os.stat(path, dir_fd=dir_fd)`, and raises `PermissionError` while the target lacks `S_IWRITE`; otherwise it calls the real `os.unlink`. `discard` removes the whole tree, and the fake saw at least one refusal.
- `os.unlink` patched to always raise `PermissionError`: `discard` returns without raising.
- `discard` on a path that does not exist returns without raising.
- Calling the hook directly with `os.open` and with `os.scandir` as `func` returns without raising and without calling them again.
- After merge: once this, plump-smelly-indianabat (which re-enables the test on Windows) and flowered-nonvalued-mink are all on main, the leak test passes in a `sweep (windows)` run on main.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `workspace.discard` removes a workspace containing read-only files on Windows semantics, proven by a test that reproduces the read-only refusal, and never raises.
- [x] `test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` passes in a `sweep (windows)` run on main.
